newsitem.title: THAILAND: First Thai copper smelter to operate from 1998.
newsitem.headline: First Thai copper smelter to operate from 1998.

text.p: Thailand's first copper smelter, developed by unlisted Thai Copper Industries, was expected to come on stream by October 1998 as scheduled, the company's top official said on Tuesday.

Company chairman and chief executive officer Prayudh Mahagitsiri told Reuters the planned full capacity of an annual 165,000 tonnes of cathodes would be reached a year after the US$600 million smelter started operating.
"The construction is proceeding at the expected pace. The project will be on target," he said.
The smelter is in eastern Rayong province.
Prayudh said he had not asked or planned to request the government for any additional help or tariff protection.
The current import duty on copper cathodes is 6.00 percent.
"We have never asked the government to increase the import duty. We are quite happy with the investment incentives we received from the Board of Investment," he said.
All the copper produced will be sold in Thailand. Local demand for copper cathode had soared to a projected 195,000 tonnes in 1996 from 30,000 tonnes in 1989, industry sources said.
